Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

"""kitty: track shared expenses on group trips."""
import sys

from .cli import main

sys.exit(main())
"""Command-line interface for kitty."""

import argparse
import csv
import json
import os
import sys

from . import core
from .core import KittyError


class _Parser(argparse.ArgumentParser):
    """ArgumentParser that reports usage errors with exit status 1."""

    def error(self, message):
        self.print_usage(sys.stderr)
        raise KittyError(message)


def _print_json(value):
    print(json.dumps(value, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Commands


def cmd_init(args):
    if os.path.exists(core.DATA_FILE):
        raise KittyError(f"{core.DATA_FILE} already exists in this directory")
    currency = core.parse_currency(args.currency)
    core.save(core.new_kitty(currency))
    print(f"Started a new kitty in {currency}")


def cmd_member_add(args, data):
    name = core.parse_name(args.name)
    if name in data["members"]:
        raise KittyError(f"{name!r} is already a member")
    data["members"].append(name)
    core.save(data)
    print(f"Added {name}")


def cmd_member_remove(args, data):
    name = core.require_member(data, args.name)
    if core.member_is_referenced(data, name):
        raise KittyError(
            f"{name} is part of recorded expenses or payments; remove those first"
        )
    data["members"].remove(name)
    core.save(data)
    print(f"Removed {name}")


def cmd_member_list(args, data):
    _print_json(data["members"])


def cmd_expense_add(args, data):
    payer = core.require_member(data, args.payer)
    amount = core.parse_amount(args.amount)
    description = " ".join(args.description).strip()
    if not description:
        raise KittyError("description cannot be empty")
    currency = core.parse_currency(args.currency) if args.currency else data["currency"]
    day = core.parse_date(args.date) if args.date else core.today()
    category = (args.category or "other").strip().lower()
    if not category:
        raise KittyError("category cannot be empty")
    rate, base_amount = core.to_base(data, amount, currency)
    shares = core.compute_shares(
        data, amount, base_amount,
        among=args.among, exact=args.exact, shares=args.shares, percent=args.percent,
    )

    expense_id = data["next_expense_id"]
    data["next_expense_id"] += 1
    data["expenses"].append({
        "id": expense_id,
        "seq": core.next_seq(data),
        "date": day,
        "payer": payer,
        "description": description,
        "amount": core.money(amount),
        "currency": currency,
        "rate": str(rate),
        "base_amount": core.money(base_amount),
        "category": category,
        "shares": {name: core.money(share) for name, share in shares.items()},
    })
    core.save(data)
    print(expense_id)


def cmd_expense_list(args, data):
    _print_json([core.expense_view(e) for e in core.sorted_records(data["expenses"])])


def _remove_by_id(records, text, kind):
    try:
        record_id = int(text)
    except ValueError:
        raise KittyError(f"invalid {kind} id: {text!r}")
    for i, r in enumerate(records):
        if r["id"] == record_id:
            return records.pop(i)
    raise KittyError(f"no {kind} with id {record_id}")


def cmd_expense_remove(args, data):
    expense = _remove_by_id(data["expenses"], args.id, "expense")
    core.save(data)
    print(f"Removed expense {expense['id']} ({expense['description']})")


def cmd_payment_add(args, data):
    sender = core.require_member(data, args.sender)
    recipient = core.require_member(data, args.recipient)
    if sender == recipient:
        raise KittyError("a payment needs two different people")
    amount = core.parse_amount(args.amount)
    currency = core.parse_currency(args.currency) if args.currency else data["currency"]
    day = core.parse_date(args.date) if args.date else core.today()
    rate, base_amount = core.to_base(data, amount, currency)

    payment_id = data["next_payment_id"]
    data["next_payment_id"] += 1
    data["payments"].append({
        "id": payment_id,
        "seq": core.next_seq(data),
        "date": day,
        "from": sender,
        "to": recipient,
        "amount": core.money(amount),
        "currency": currency,
        "rate": str(rate),
        "base_amount": core.money(base_amount),
    })
    core.save(data)
    print(payment_id)


def cmd_payment_list(args, data):
    _print_json([core.payment_view(p) for p in core.sorted_records(data["payments"])])


def cmd_payment_remove(args, data):
    payment = _remove_by_id(data["payments"], args.id, "payment")
    core.save(data)
    print(f"Removed payment {payment['id']} ({payment['from']} to {payment['to']})")


def cmd_rate_set(args, data):
    currency = core.parse_currency(args.currency)
    if currency == data["currency"]:
        raise KittyError(f"{currency} is the base currency; its rate is always 1")
    rate = core.parse_number(args.rate, "rate")
    data["rates"][currency] = str(rate)
    core.save(data)
    print(f"1 {currency} = {rate} {data['currency']}")


def cmd_balances(args, data):
    _print_json({name: core.money(b) for name, b in core.balances(data).items()})


def cmd_settle(args, data):
    _print_json(core.settle(data))


def cmd_history(args, data):
    name = core.require_member(data, args.name)
    _print_json(core.history(data, name))


def cmd_report(args, data):
    _print_json(core.report(data))


def cmd_export(args, data):
    columns = ["id", "date", "payer", "description", "amount", "currency", "category", "base_amount"]
    try:
        with open(args.file, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            writer = csv.writer(f)
            writer.writerow(columns)
            for e in core.sorted_records(data["expenses"]):
                writer.writerow([e[c] for c in columns])
    except OSError as e:
        raise KittyError(f"cannot write {args.file}: {e}")
    print(f"Exported {len(data['expenses'])} expenses to {args.file}")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Argument parsing


def build_parser():
    parser = _Parser(prog="python3 -m kitty", description="Track shared expenses on group trips.")
    commands = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", metavar="COMMAND", parser_class=_Parser)
    commands.required = True

    p = commands.add_parser("init", help="start a new kitty in this directory")
    p.add_argument("currency", help="base currency, e.g. EUR")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_init, needs_data=False)

    member = commands.add_parser("member", help="manage group members")
    member_cmds = member.add_subparsers(dest="action", metavar="ACTION", parser_class=_Parser)
    member_cmds.required = True
    p = member_cmds.add_parser("add", help="add a member")
    p.add_argument("name")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_member_add)
    p = member_cmds.add_parser("remove", help="remove a member with no recorded activity")
    p.add_argument("name")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_member_remove)
    p = member_cmds.add_parser("list", help="list members as JSON")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_member_list)

    expense = commands.add_parser("expense", help="record and manage expenses")
    expense_cmds = expense.add_subparsers(dest="action", metavar="ACTION", parser_class=_Parser)
    expense_cmds.required = True
    p = expense_cmds.add_parser("add", help="record an expense and print its id")
    p.add_argument("payer")
    p.add_argument("amount")
    p.add_argument("description", nargs="+")
    p.add_argument("--among", metavar="A,B", help="split equally among only these people")
    p.add_argument("--exact", metavar="A=30,B=20", help="split by exact amounts")
    p.add_argument("--shares", metavar="A=2,B=1", help="split by shares")
    p.add_argument("--percent", metavar="A=60,B=40", help="split by percentages")
    p.add_argument("--currency", help="currency paid in (default: base currency)")
    p.add_argument("--date", metavar="YYYY-MM-DD", help="date of the expense (default: today)")
    p.add_argument("--category", help="category (default: other)")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_expense_add)
    p = expense_cmds.add_parser("list", help="list expenses as JSON")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_expense_list)
    p = expense_cmds.add_parser("remove", help="remove an expense")
    p.add_argument("id")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_expense_remove)

    payment = commands.add_parser("payment", help="record and manage repayments")
    payment_cmds = payment.add_subparsers(dest="action", metavar="ACTION", parser_class=_Parser)
    payment_cmds.required = True
    p = payment_cmds.add_parser("add", help="record a payment and print its id")
    p.add_argument("sender", metavar="FROM")
    p.add_argument("recipient", metavar="TO")
    p.add_argument("amount")
    p.add_argument("--currency", help="currency paid in (default: base currency)")
    p.add_argument("--date", metavar="YYYY-MM-DD", help="date of the payment (default: today)")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_payment_add)
    p = payment_cmds.add_parser("list", help="list payments as JSON")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_payment_list)
    p = payment_cmds.add_parser("remove", help="remove a payment")
    p.add_argument("id")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_payment_remove)

    rate = commands.add_parser("rate", help="manage exchange rates")
    rate_cmds = rate.add_subparsers(dest="action", metavar="ACTION", parser_class=_Parser)
    rate_cmds.required = True
    p = rate_cmds.add_parser("set", help="set what one unit of CURRENCY is worth in the base currency")
    p.add_argument("currency")
    p.add_argument("rate")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_rate_set)

"""Storage, validation and money calculations for kitty.

All money is handled as Decimal and rounded to cents. Every expense stores its
amount converted to the base currency (using the rate in force when it was
added) together with each person's share, and the shares always add up to the
base amount exactly, so balances always sum to zero.
"""

import json
import os
import re
import tempfile
from datetime import date
from decimal import ROUND_FLOOR, ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal, InvalidOperation

DATA_FILE = "kitty.json"
CENT = Decimal("0.01")
FORMAT_VERSION = 1

_NUMBER_RE = re.compile(r"^(\d{1,15}(\.\d+)?|\.\d+)$")
_DATE_RE = re.compile(r"^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$")
_CURRENCY_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-Z]{3}$")


class KittyError(Exception):
    """A problem caused by user input or the data file, reported without a traceback."""


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Parsing and formatting


def money(value):
    """Format a Decimal as a string with two decimals."""
    return str(value.quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP))


def parse_number(text, what, allow_zero=False):
    """Parse a non-negative plain decimal number such as '12', '0.5' or '33.33'."""
    text = text.strip()
    if not _NUMBER_RE.match(text):
        raise KittyError(f"invalid {what}: {text!r} (expected a positive number like 12.50)")
    try:
        value = Decimal(text)
    except InvalidOperation:
        raise KittyError(f"invalid {what}: {text!r}")
    if value == 0 and not allow_zero:
        raise KittyError(f"invalid {what}: {text!r} (must be greater than zero)")
    return value


def parse_amount(text, what="amount", allow_zero=False):
    """Parse a money amount: a positive number with at most two decimals."""
    value = parse_number(text, what, allow_zero)
    if value != value.quantize(CENT):
        raise KittyError(f"invalid {what}: {text!r} (at most two decimal places)")
    return value.quantize(CENT)


def parse_date(text):
    if not _DATE_RE.match(text):
        raise KittyError(f"invalid date: {text!r} (expected YYYY-MM-DD)")
    try:
        date.fromisoformat(text)
    except ValueError:
        raise KittyError(f"invalid date: {text!r}")
    return text


def parse_currency(text):
    code = text.strip().upper()
    if not _CURRENCY_RE.match(code):
        raise KittyError(f"invalid currency: {text!r} (expected a 3-letter code like USD)")
    return code


def parse_name(text):
    name = text.strip()
    if not name:
        raise KittyError("member name cannot be empty")
    if "," in name or "=" in name:
        raise KittyError(f"invalid member name: {text!r} (names cannot contain ',' or '=')")
    if name.startswith("-"):
        raise KittyError(f"invalid member name: {text!r} (names cannot start with '-')")
    return name


def today():
    return date.today().isoformat()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Storage


def new_kitty(currency):
    return {
        "version": FORMAT_VERSION,
        "currency": currency,
        "members": [],
        "rates": {},
        "expenses": [],
        "payments": [],
        "next_expense_id": 1,
        "next_payment_id": 1,
        "next_seq": 1,
    }


def load(path=DATA_FILE):
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        raise KittyError(f"no {path} in this directory; run 'init CURRENCY' first")
    try:
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            data = json.load(f)
    except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
        raise KittyError(f"cannot read {path}: {e}")
    if not isinstance(data, dict) or data.get("version") != FORMAT_VERSION:
        raise KittyError(f"{path} is not a kitty file this version understands")
    return data


def save(data, path=DATA_FILE):
    """Write atomically so an interrupted save never leaves a half-written file."""
    directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path))
    try:
        fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=".kitty-", suffix=".json", dir=directory)
        try:
            with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                json.dump(data, f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
                f.write("\n")
            os.replace(tmp, path)
        except BaseException:
            os.unlink(tmp)
            raise
    except OSError as e:
        raise KittyError(f"cannot write {path}: {e}")


def next_seq(data):
    """Global creation counter, used to order records that share a date."""
    seq = data["next_seq"]
    data["next_seq"] += 1
    return seq


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Members


def require_member(data, name):
    if name not in data["members"]:
        raise KittyError(f"unknown member: {name!r}")
    return name


def member_is_referenced(data, name):
    for e in data["expenses"]:
        if e["payer"] == name or name in e["shares"]:
            return True
    for p in data["payments"]:
        if name in (p["from"], p["to"]):
            return True
    return False


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Currency


def to_base(data, amount, currency):
    """Return (rate, base_amount) for an amount in the given currency."""
    if currency == data["currency"]:
        return Decimal(1), amount
    if currency not in data["rates"]:
        raise KittyError(
            f"no exchange rate for {currency}; run 'rate set {currency} RATE' first"
        )
    rate = Decimal(data["rates"][currency])
    return rate, (amount * rate).quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Splitting


def allocate(total, weights):
    """Split total in proportion to weights so the parts add up to total exactly.

    weights is a list of (name, Decimal). Each part is its exact portion rounded
    down to the cent; the leftover cents then go one each to the names in the
    order given.
    """
    cents = int(total / CENT)
    weight_sum = sum(w for _, w in weights)
    parts = []
    for name, w in weights:
        exact = Decimal(cents) * w / weight_sum
        parts.append([name, int(exact.to_integral_value(rounding=ROUND_FLOOR))])
    leftover = cents - sum(c for _, c in parts)
    for part in parts[:leftover]:
        part[1] += 1
    return {name: Decimal(c) * CENT for name, c in parts}


def parse_name_list(data, text):
    names = [n.strip() for n in text.split(",")]
    if not text.strip() or any(not n for n in names):
        raise KittyError(f"invalid member list: {text!r} (expected A,B,...)")
    seen = set()
    for n in names:
        require_member(data, n)
        if n in seen:
            raise KittyError(f"{n!r} is listed more than once")
        seen.add(n)
    return names


def parse_weights(data, text, option, parse_value):
    """Parse 'A=30,B=20' into [(name, Decimal), ...]."""
    result = []
    seen = set()
    for item in text.split(","):
        name, sep, value = item.partition("=")
        name = name.strip()
        if not sep or not name or not value.strip():
            raise KittyError(f"invalid {option} entry: {item.strip()!r} (expected NAME=VALUE)")
        require_member(data, name)
        if name in seen:
            raise KittyError(f"{name!r} is listed more than once in {option}")
        seen.add(name)
        result.append((name, parse_value(value)))
    if sum(w for _, w in result) == 0:
        raise KittyError(f"{option} values cannot all be zero")
    return result


def compute_shares(data, amount, base_amount, among=None, exact=None, shares=None, percent=None):
    """Return {name: Decimal share in base currency} for a new expense."""
    given = [opt for opt, v in (("--among", among), ("--exact", exact),
                                ("--shares", shares), ("--percent", percent)) if v is not None]
    if len(given) > 1:
        raise KittyError(f"use only one of {', '.join(given)}")

    if exact is not None:
        weights = parse_weights(
            data, exact, "--exact", lambda v: parse_amount(v, "--exact amount", allow_zero=True)
        )
        total = sum(w for _, w in weights)
        if total != amount:
            raise KittyError(
                f"--exact amounts add up to {money(total)}, not the expense amount {money(amount)}"
            )
    elif shares is not None:
        weights = parse_weights(
            data, shares, "--shares", lambda v: parse_number(v, "--shares value", allow_zero=True)
        )
    elif percent is not None:
        weights = parse_weights(
            data, percent, "--percent", lambda v: parse_number(v, "--percent value", allow_zero=True)
        )
        total = sum(w for _, w in weights)
        if total != 100:
            raise KittyError(f"--percent values add up to {total}, not 100")
    else:
        names = parse_name_list(data, among) if among is not None else list(data["members"])
        if not names:
            raise KittyError("there are no members to split this expense among; add some first")
        weights = [(n, Decimal(1)) for n in names]

    return allocate(base_amount, weights)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Reports


def sorted_records(records):
    """Sort expenses or payments by date, then by id."""
    return sorted(records, key=lambda r: (r["date"], r["id"]))


def _ordered_names(data, names):
    """Members in the order they were added, followed by anyone else alphabetically."""
    known = [m for m in data["members"] if m in names]
    return known + sorted(n for n in names if n not in data["members"])


def balances(data):
    totals = {m: Decimal(0) for m in data["members"]}
    for e in data["expenses"]:
        totals[e["payer"]] = totals.get(e["payer"], Decimal(0)) + Decimal(e["base_amount"])
        for name, share in e["shares"].items():
            totals[name] = totals.get(name, Decimal(0)) - Decimal(share)
    for p in data["payments"]:
        amount = Decimal(p["base_amount"])
        totals[p["from"]] = totals.get(p["from"], Decimal(0)) + amount
        totals[p["to"]] = totals.get(p["to"], Decimal(0)) - amount
    return {n: totals[n] for n in _ordered_names(data, totals)}


def settle(data):
    """Suggest payments that bring every balance to zero.

    Repeatedly has the person who owes the most pay the person owed the most,
    which needs at most one payment fewer than the number of people. Ties go to
    whoever comes first alphabetically, ignoring case.
    """
    cents = {n: int(b / CENT) for n, b in balances(data).items()}
    transfers = []
    while True:
        debtors = [n for n, c in cents.items() if c < 0]
        creditors = [n for n, c in cents.items() if c > 0]
        if not debtors or not creditors:
            break
        debtor = min(debtors, key=lambda n: (cents[n], n.casefold(), n))
        creditor = min(creditors, key=lambda n: (-cents[n], n.casefold(), n))
        amount = min(-cents[debtor], cents[creditor])
        cents[debtor] += amount
        cents[creditor] -= amount
        transfers.append({"from": debtor, "to": creditor, "amount": money(Decimal(amount) * CENT)})
    return transfers


def history(data, name):
    events = []
    for e in data["expenses"]:
        change = Decimal(0)
        if e["payer"] == name:
            change += Decimal(e["base_amount"])
        if name in e["shares"]:
            change -= Decimal(e["shares"][name])
        if e["payer"] == name or name in e["shares"]:
            events.append((e["date"], e["seq"], e["description"], change))
    for p in data["payments"]:
        amount = Decimal(p["base_amount"])
        if p["from"] == name:
            events.append((p["date"], p["seq"], f"Payment to {p['to']}", amount))
        elif p["to"] == name:
            events.append((p["date"], p["seq"], f"Payment from {p['from']}", -amount))
    events.sort(key=lambda ev: (ev[0], ev[1]))

    result = []
    running = Decimal(0)
    for day, _, description, change in events:
        running += change
        result.append({
            "date": day,
            "description": description,
            "change": money(change),
            "balance": money(running),
        })
    return result


def report(data):
    totals = {}
    for e in data["expenses"]:
        category = totals.setdefault(e["category"], {})
        for name, share in e["shares"].items():
            category[name] = category.get(name, Decimal(0)) + Decimal(share)
    return {
        cat: {n: money(totals[cat][n]) for n in _ordered_names(data, totals[cat])}
        for cat in sorted(totals)
    }


def expense_view(e):
    return {
        "id": e["id"],
        "date": e["date"],
        "payer": e["payer"],
        "description": e["description"],
        "amount": e["amount"],
        "currency": e["currency"],
        "base_amount": e["base_amount"],
        "category": e["category"],
        "shares": dict(e["shares"]),
    }

        "to": p["to"],
        "amount": p["amount"],

import os

DATA_FILE = "kitty.json"
CENT = Decimal("0.01")

_NUMBER_RE = re.compile(r"^(\d{1,15}(\.\d+)?|\.\d+)$")
_DATE_RE = re.compile(r"^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$")

    """Parse a non-negative plain decimal number such as '12', '0.5' or '33.33'."""
    text = text.strip()

        raise KittyError(f"invalid {what}: {text!r} (expected a positive number like 12.50)")
    try:
        value = Decimal(text)
    except InvalidOperation:
        raise KittyError(f"invalid {what}: {text!r}")
    if value == 0 and not allow_zero:
        raise KittyError(f"invalid {what}: {text!r} (must be greater than zero)")
    return value

    """Parse a money amount: a positive number with at most two decimals."""
    value = parse_number(text, what, allow_zero)
    if value != value.quantize(CENT):
        raise KittyError(f"invalid {what}: {text!r} (at most two decimal places)")
    return value.quantize(CENT)

        raise KittyError(f"invalid date: {text!r} (expected YYYY-MM-DD)")

    except ValueError:
        raise KittyError(f"invalid date: {text!r}")
    return text


def parse_currency(text):
    code = text.strip().upper()
    if not _CURRENCY_RE.match(code):
        raise KittyError(f"invalid currency: {text!r} (expected a 3-letter code like USD)")
    return code

    name = text.strip()
    if not name:
        raise KittyError("member name cannot be empty")
    if "," in name or "=" in name:
        raise KittyError(f"invalid member name: {text!r} (names cannot contain ',' or '=')")
    if name.startswith("-"):
        raise KittyError(f"invalid member name: {text!r} (names cannot start with '-')")

def new_kitty(currency):

        "version": FORMAT_VERSION,
        "currency": currency,
        "members": [],
        "rates": {},

        "payments": [],

    except (OSError, ValueError) as e:

    cents = int(total / CENT)
    weight_sum = sum(w for _, w in weights)
    parts = []
    for name, w in weights:
        exact = Decimal(cents) * w / weight_sum
        parts.append([name, int(exact.to_integral_value(rounding=ROUND_FLOOR))])
    leftover = cents - sum(c for _, c in parts)
    for part in parts[:leftover]:
        part[1] += 1

    seen = set()
    for n in names:

        if n in seen:

    result = []
    seen = set()
    for item in text.split(","):
        name, sep, value = item.partition("=")
        name = name.strip()
        if not sep or not name or not value.strip():
            raise KittyError(f"invalid {option} entry: {item.strip()!r} (expected NAME=VALUE)")
        require_member(data, name)

            raise KittyError(f"{name!r} is listed more than once in {option}")

    """Return {name: Decimal share in base currency} for a new expense."""
    given = [opt for opt, v in (("--among", among), ("--exact", exact),

    if len(given) > 1:

            data, shares, "--shares", lambda v: parse_number(v, "--shares value", allow_zero=True)

    known = [m for m in data["members"] if m in names]

    totals = {m: Decimal(0) for m in data["members"]}
    for e in data["expenses"]:
        totals[e["payer"]] = totals.get(e["payer"], Decimal(0)) + Decimal(e["base_amount"])
        for name, share in e["shares"].items():
            totals[name] = totals.get(name, Decimal(0)) - Decimal(share)
    for p in data["payments"]:
        amount = Decimal(p["base_amount"])
        totals[p["from"]] = totals.get(p["from"], Decimal(0)) + amount
        totals[p["to"]] = totals.get(p["to"], Decimal(0)) - amount

    """Suggest payments that bring every balance to zero.

    Repeatedly has the person who owes the most pay the person owed the most,
    which needs at most one payment fewer than the number of people. Ties go to
    whoever comes first alphabetically, ignoring case.

    cents = {n: int(b / CENT) for n, b in balances(data).items()}

        creditors = [n for n, c in cents.items() if c > 0]

"""kitty: track shared expenses on group trips."""

"""Command-line interface for kitty."""

import argparse
import csv
import json
import os
import sys

from . import core
from .core import KittyError


class _Parser(argparse.ArgumentParser):
    """ArgumentParser that reports usage errors with exit status 1."""

    def error(self, message):
        self.print_usage(sys.stderr)
        raise KittyError(message)


def _print_json(value):
    print(json.dumps(value, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Commands


def cmd_init(args):
    if os.path.exists(core.DATA_FILE):
        raise KittyError(f"{core.DATA_FILE} already exists in this directory")
    currency = core.parse_currency(args.currency)
    core.save(core.new_kitty(currency))
    print(f"Started a new kitty in {currency}")


def cmd_member_add(args, data):
    name = core.parse_name(args.name)
    if name in data["members"]:
        raise KittyError(f"{name!r} is already a member")
    data["members"].append(name)
    core.save(data)
    print(f"Added {name}")


def cmd_member_remove(args, data):
    name = core.require_member(data, args.name)
    if core.member_is_referenced(data, name):
        raise KittyError(
            f"{name} is part of recorded expenses or payments; remove those first"
        )
    data["members"].remove(name)
    core.save(data)
    print(f"Removed {name}")


def cmd_member_list(args, data):
    _print_json(data["members"])


def cmd_expense_add(args, data):
    payer = core.require_member(data, args.payer)
    amount = core.parse_amount(args.amount)
    description = " ".join(args.description).strip()
    if not description:
        raise KittyError("description cannot be empty")
    currency = core.parse_currency(args.currency) if args.currency else data["currency"]
    day = core.parse_date(args.date) if args.date else core.today()
    category = (args.category or "other").strip().lower()
    if not category:
        raise KittyError("category cannot be empty")
    rate, base_amount = core.to_base(data, amount, currency)
    shares = core.compute_shares(
        data, amount, base_amount,
        among=args.among, exact=args.exact, shares=args.shares, percent=args.percent,
    )

    expense_id = data["next_expense_id"]
    data["next_expense_id"] += 1
    data["expenses"].append({
        "id": expense_id,
        "seq": core.next_seq(data),
        "date": day,
        "payer": payer,
        "description": description,
        "amount": core.money(amount),
        "currency": currency,
        "rate": str(rate),
        "base_amount": core.money(base_amount),
        "category": category,
        "shares": {name: core.money(share) for name, share in shares.items()},
    })
    core.save(data)
    print(expense_id)


def cmd_expense_list(args, data):
    _print_json([core.expense_view(e) for e in core.sorted_records(data["expenses"])])


def _remove_by_id(records, text, kind):
    try:
        record_id = int(text)
    except ValueError:
        raise KittyError(f"invalid {kind} id: {text!r}")
    for i, r in enumerate(records):
        if r["id"] == record_id:
            return records.pop(i)
    raise KittyError(f"no {kind} with id {record_id}")


def cmd_expense_remove(args, data):
    expense = _remove_by_id(data["expenses"], args.id, "expense")
    core.save(data)
    print(f"Removed expense {expense['id']} ({expense['description']})")


def cmd_payment_add(args, data):
    sender = core.require_member(data, args.sender)
    recipient = core.require_member(data, args.recipient)
    if sender == recipient:
        raise KittyError("a payment needs two different people")
    amount = core.parse_amount(args.amount)
    currency = core.parse_currency(args.currency) if args.currency else data["currency"]
    day = core.parse_date(args.date) if args.date else core.today()
    rate, base_amount = core.to_base(data, amount, currency)

    payment_id = data["next_payment_id"]
    data["next_payment_id"] += 1
    data["payments"].append({
        "id": payment_id,
        "seq": core.next_seq(data),
        "date": day,
        "from": sender,
        "to": recipient,
        "amount": core.money(amount),
        "currency": currency,
        "rate": str(rate),
        "base_amount": core.money(base_amount),
    })
    core.save(data)
    print(payment_id)


def cmd_payment_list(args, data):
    _print_json([core.payment_view(p) for p in core.sorted_records(data["payments"])])


def cmd_payment_remove(args, data):
    payment = _remove_by_id(data["payments"], args.id, "payment")
    core.save(data)
    print(f"Removed payment {payment['id']} ({payment['from']} to {payment['to']})")


def cmd_rate_set(args, data):
    currency = core.parse_currency(args.currency)
    if currency == data["currency"]:
        raise KittyError(f"{currency} is the base currency; its rate is always 1")
    rate = core.parse_number(args.rate, "rate")
    data["rates"][currency] = str(rate)
    core.save(data)
    print(f"1 {currency} = {rate} {data['currency']}")


def cmd_balances(args, data):
    _print_json({name: core.money(b) for name, b in core.balances(data).items()})


def cmd_settle(args, data):
    _print_json(core.settle(data))


def cmd_history(args, data):
    name = core.require_member(data, args.name)
    _print_json(core.history(data, name))


def cmd_report(args, data):
    _print_json(core.report(data))


def cmd_export(args, data):
    columns = ["id", "date", "payer", "description", "amount", "currency", "category", "base_amount"]
    try:
        with open(args.file, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            writer = csv.writer(f)
            writer.writerow(columns)
            for e in core.sorted_records(data["expenses"]):
                writer.writerow([e[c] for c in columns])
    except OSError as e:
        raise KittyError(f"cannot write {args.file}: {e}")
    print(f"Exported {len(data['expenses'])} expenses to {args.file}")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Argument parsing


def build_parser():
    parser = _Parser(prog="python3 -m kitty", description="Track shared expenses on group trips.")
    commands = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", metavar="COMMAND", parser_class=_Parser)
    commands.required = True

    p = commands.add_parser("init", help="start a new kitty in this directory")
    p.add_argument("currency", help="base currency, e.g. EUR")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_init, needs_data=False)

    member = commands.add_parser("member", help="manage group members")
    member_cmds = member.add_subparsers(dest="action", metavar="ACTION", parser_class=_Parser)
    member_cmds.required = True
    p = member_cmds.add_parser("add", help="add a member")
    p.add_argument("name")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_member_add)
    p = member_cmds.add_parser("remove", help="remove a member with no recorded activity")
    p.add_argument("name")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_member_remove)
    p = member_cmds.add_parser("list", help="list members as JSON")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_member_list)

    expense = commands.add_parser("expense", help="record and manage expenses")
    expense_cmds = expense.add_subparsers(dest="action", metavar="ACTION", parser_class=_Parser)
    expense_cmds.required = True
    p = expense_cmds.add_parser("add", help="record an expense and print its id")
    p.add_argument("payer")
    p.add_argument("amount")
    p.add_argument("description", nargs="+")
    p.add_argument("--among", metavar="A,B", help="split equally among only these people")
    p.add_argument("--exact", metavar="A=30,B=20", help="split by exact amounts")
    p.add_argument("--shares", metavar="A=2,B=1", help="split by shares")
    p.add_argument("--percent", metavar="A=60,B=40", help="split by percentages")
    p.add_argument("--currency", help="currency paid in (default: base currency)")
    p.add_argument("--date", metavar="YYYY-MM-DD", help="date of the expense (default: today)")
    p.add_argument("--category", help="category (default: other)")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_expense_add)
    p = expense_cmds.add_parser("list", help="list expenses as JSON")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_expense_list)
    p = expense_cmds.add_parser("remove", help="remove an expense")
    p.add_argument("id")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_expense_remove)

    payment = commands.add_parser("payment", help="record and manage repayments")
    payment_cmds = payment.add_subparsers(dest="action", metavar="ACTION", parser_class=_Parser)
    payment_cmds.required = True
    p = payment_cmds.add_parser("add", help="record a payment and print its id")
    p.add_argument("sender", metavar="FROM")
    p.add_argument("recipient", metavar="TO")
    p.add_argument("amount")
    p.add_argument("--currency", help="currency paid in (default: base currency)")
    p.add_argument("--date", metavar="YYYY-MM-DD", help="date of the payment (default: today)")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_payment_add)
    p = payment_cmds.add_parser("list", help="list payments as JSON")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_payment_list)
    p = payment_cmds.add_parser("remove", help="remove a payment")
    p.add_argument("id")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_payment_remove)

    rate = commands.add_parser("rate", help="manage exchange rates")
    rate_cmds = rate.add_subparsers(dest="action", metavar="ACTION", parser_class=_Parser)
    rate_cmds.required = True
    p = rate_cmds.add_parser("set", help="set what one unit of CURRENCY is worth in the base currency")
    p.add_argument("currency")
    p.add_argument("rate")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_rate_set)

    p = commands.add_parser("balances", help="show each person's balance as JSON")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_balances)
    p = commands.add_parser("settle", help="suggest payments that square everyone up")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_settle)
    p = commands.add_parser("history", help="show everything that affected one person")
    p.add_argument("name")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_history)
    p = commands.add_parser("report", help="show each person's spending per category")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_report)
    p = commands.add_parser("export", help="write expenses to a CSV file")
    p.add_argument("file")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_export)

    return parser


def main(argv=None):
    try:
        args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
        if getattr(args, "needs_data", True):
            args.func(args, core.load())
        else:
            args.func(args)
    except KittyError as e:
        print(f"error: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    return 0
"""Storage, validation and money calculations for kitty.

All money is handled as Decimal and rounded to cents. Every expense stores its
amount converted to the base currency (using the rate in force when it was
added) together with each person's share, and the shares always add up to the
base amount exactly, so balances always sum to zero.
"""

import json
import os
import re
import tempfile
from datetime import date
from decimal import ROUND_FLOOR, ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal, InvalidOperation

DATA_FILE = "kitty.json"
CENT = Decimal("0.01")
FORMAT_VERSION = 1

_NUMBER_RE = re.compile(r"^(\d{1,15}(\.\d+)?|\.\d+)$")
_DATE_RE = re.compile(r"^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$")
_CURRENCY_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-Z]{3}$")


class KittyError(Exception):
    """A problem caused by user input or the data file, reported without a traceback."""


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Parsing and formatting


def money(value):
    """Format a Decimal as a string with two decimals."""
    return str(value.quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP))


def parse_number(text, what, allow_zero=False):
    """Parse a non-negative plain decimal number such as '12', '0.5' or '33.33'."""
    text = text.strip()
    if not _NUMBER_RE.match(text):
        raise KittyError(f"invalid {what}: {text!r} (expected a positive number like 12.50)")
    try:
        value = Decimal(text)
    except InvalidOperation:
        raise KittyError(f"invalid {what}: {text!r}")
    if value == 0 and not allow_zero:
        raise KittyError(f"invalid {what}: {text!r} (must be greater than zero)")
    return value


def parse_amount(text, what="amount", allow_zero=False):
    """Parse a money amount: a positive number with at most two decimals."""
    value = parse_number(text, what, allow_zero)
    if value != value.quantize(CENT):
        raise KittyError(f"invalid {what}: {text!r} (at most two decimal places)")
    return value.quantize(CENT)


def parse_date(text):
    if not _DATE_RE.match(text):
        raise KittyError(f"invalid date: {text!r} (expected YYYY-MM-DD)")
    try:
        date.fromisoformat(text)
    except ValueError:
        raise KittyError(f"invalid date: {text!r}")
    return text


def parse_currency(text):
    code = text.strip().upper()
    if not _CURRENCY_RE.match(code):
        raise KittyError(f"invalid currency: {text!r} (expected a 3-letter code like USD)")
    return code


def parse_name(text):
    name = text.strip()
    if not name:
        raise KittyError("member name cannot be empty")
    if "," in name or "=" in name:
        raise KittyError(f"invalid member name: {text!r} (names cannot contain ',' or '=')")
    if name.startswith("-"):
        raise KittyError(f"invalid member name: {text!r} (names cannot start with '-')")
    return name


def today():
    return date.today().isoformat()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Storage


def new_kitty(currency):
    return {
        "version": FORMAT_VERSION,
        "currency": currency,
        "members": [],
        "rates": {},
        "expenses": [],
        "payments": [],
        "next_expense_id": 1,
        "next_payment_id": 1,
        "next_seq": 1,
    }


def load(path=DATA_FILE):
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        raise KittyError(f"no {path} in this directory; run 'init CURRENCY' first")
    try:
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            data = json.load(f)
    except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
        raise KittyError(f"cannot read {path}: {e}")
    if not isinstance(data, dict) or data.get("version") != FORMAT_VERSION:
        raise KittyError(f"{path} is not a kitty file this version understands")
    return data


def save(data, path=DATA_FILE):
    """Write atomically so an interrupted save never leaves a half-written file."""
    directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path))
    try:
        fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=".kitty-", suffix=".json", dir=directory)
        try:
            with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                json.dump(data, f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
                f.write("\n")
            os.replace(tmp, path)
        except BaseException:
            os.unlink(tmp)
            raise
    except OSError as e:
        raise KittyError(f"cannot write {path}: {e}")


def next_seq(data):
    """Global creation counter, used to order records that share a date."""
    seq = data["next_seq"]
    data["next_seq"] += 1
    return seq


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Members


def require_member(data, name):
    if name not in data["members"]:
        raise KittyError(f"unknown member: {name!r}")
    return name


def member_is_referenced(data, name):
    for e in data["expenses"]:
        if e["payer"] == name or name in e["shares"]:
            return True
    for p in data["payments"]:
        if name in (p["from"], p["to"]):
            return True
    return False


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Currency


def to_base(data, amount, currency):
    """Return (rate, base_amount) for an amount in the given currency."""
    if currency == data["currency"]:
        return Decimal(1), amount
    if currency not in data["rates"]:
        raise KittyError(
            f"no exchange rate for {currency}; run 'rate set {currency} RATE' first"
        )
    rate = Decimal(data["rates"][currency])
    return rate, (amount * rate).quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Splitting


def allocate(total, weights):
    """Split total in proportion to weights so the parts add up to total exactly.

    weights is a list of (name, Decimal). Each part is its exact portion rounded
    down to the cent; the leftover cents then go one each to the names in the
    order given.
    """
    cents = int(total / CENT)
    weight_sum = sum(w for _, w in weights)
    parts = []
    for name, w in weights:
        exact = Decimal(cents) * w / weight_sum
        parts.append([name, int(exact.to_integral_value(rounding=ROUND_FLOOR))])
    leftover = cents - sum(c for _, c in parts)
    for part in parts[:leftover]:
        part[1] += 1
    return {name: Decimal(c) * CENT for name, c in parts}


def parse_name_list(data, text):
    names = [n.strip() for n in text.split(",")]
    if not text.strip() or any(not n for n in names):
        raise KittyError(f"invalid member list: {text!r} (expected A,B,...)")
    seen = set()
    for n in names:
        require_member(data, n)
        if n in seen:
            raise KittyError(f"{n!r} is listed more than once")
        seen.add(n)
    return names


def parse_weights(data, text, option, parse_value):
    """Parse 'A=30,B=20' into [(name, Decimal), ...]."""
    result = []
    seen = set()
    for item in text.split(","):
        name, sep, value = item.partition("=")
        name = name.strip()
        if not sep or not name or not value.strip():
            raise KittyError(f"invalid {option} entry: {item.strip()!r} (expected NAME=VALUE)")
        require_member(data, name)
        if name in seen:
            raise KittyError(f"{name!r} is listed more than once in {option}")
        seen.add(name)
        result.append((name, parse_value(value)))
    if sum(w for _, w in result) == 0:
        raise KittyError(f"{option} values cannot all be zero")
    return result


def compute_shares(data, amount, base_amount, among=None, exact=None, shares=None, percent=None):
    """Return {name: Decimal share in base currency} for a new expense."""
    given = [opt for opt, v in (("--among", among), ("--exact", exact),
                                ("--shares", shares), ("--percent", percent)) if v is not None]
    if len(given) > 1:
        raise KittyError(f"use only one of {', '.join(given)}")

    if exact is not None:
        weights = parse_weights(
            data, exact, "--exact", lambda v: parse_amount(v, "--exact amount", allow_zero=True)
        )
        total = sum(w for _, w in weights)
        if total != amount:
            raise KittyError(
                f"--exact amounts add up to {money(total)}, not the expense amount {money(amount)}"
            )
    elif shares is not None:
        weights = parse_weights(
            data, shares, "--shares", lambda v: parse_number(v, "--shares value", allow_zero=True)
        )
    elif percent is not None:
        weights = parse_weights(
            data, percent, "--percent", lambda v: parse_number(v, "--percent value", allow_zero=True)
        )
        total = sum(w for _, w in weights)
        if total != 100:
            raise KittyError(f"--percent values add up to {total}, not 100")
    else:
        names = parse_name_list(data, among) if among is not None else list(data["members"])
        if not names:
            raise KittyError("there are no members to split this expense among; add some first")
        weights = [(n, Decimal(1)) for n in names]

    return allocate(base_amount, weights)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Reports


def sorted_records(records):
    """Sort expenses or payments by date, then by id."""
    return sorted(records, key=lambda r: (r["date"], r["id"]))


def _ordered_names(data, names):
    """Members in the order they were added, followed by anyone else alphabetically."""
    known = [m for m in data["members"] if m in names]
    return known + sorted(n for n in names if n not in data["members"])


def balances(data):
    totals = {m: Decimal(0) for m in data["members"]}
    for e in data["expenses"]:
        totals[e["payer"]] = totals.get(e["payer"], Decimal(0)) + Decimal(e["base_amount"])
        for name, share in e["shares"].items():
            totals[name] = totals.get(name, Decimal(0)) - Decimal(share)
    for p in data["payments"]:
        amount = Decimal(p["base_amount"])
        totals[p["from"]] = totals.get(p["from"], Decimal(0)) + amount

def settle(data):
    """Suggest payments that bring every balance to zero.

    Repeatedly has the person who owes the most pay the person owed the most,
    which needs at most one payment fewer than the number of people. Ties go to
    whoever comes first alphabetically, ignoring case.
    """
    cents = {n: int(b / CENT) for n, b in balances(data).items()}
    transfers = []
    while True:
        debtors = [n for n, c in cents.items() if c < 0]
        creditors = [n for n, c in cents.items() if c > 0]
        if not debtors or not creditors:
            break
        debtor = min(debtors, key=lambda n: (cents[n], n.casefold(), n))
        creditor = min(creditors, key=lambda n: (-cents[n], n.casefold(), n))
        amount = min(-cents[debtor], cents[creditor])
        cents[debtor] += amount
        cents[creditor] -= amount
        transfers.append({"from": debtor, "to": creditor, "amount": money(Decimal(amount) * CENT)})
    return transfers


def history(data, name):
    events = []
    for e in data["expenses"]:

            change -= Decimal(e["shares"][name])
        if e["payer"] == name or name in e["shares"]:
            events.append((e["date"], e["seq"], e["description"], change))
    for p in data["payments"]:
        amount = Decimal(p["base_amount"])
        if p["from"] == name:
            events.append((p["date"], p["seq"], f"Payment to {p['to']}", amount))
        elif p["to"] == name:
            events.append((p["date"], p["seq"], f"Payment from {p['from']}", -amount))

    result = []
    running = Decimal(0)
    for day, _, description, change in events:
        running += change
        result.append({
            "date": day,
            "description": description,
            "change": money(change),
            "balance": money(running),

    return result

content.text:
I've added `expense edit ID` and the `--in CUR` option for `balances` and `settle`. All 61 tests pass: the 47 that were already there, plus 14 new ones in `tests/test_kitty.py` for these features. The sandbox wouldn't let me make a scratch folder to run the CLI by hand, so the tests are the only check besides the `-h` output.

**`expense edit ID`**
- Takes `--payer`, `--amount`, `--description`, `--date`, `--category` and `--currency`, plus at most one of `--among`, `--exact`, `--shares` or `--percent`. Only the parts you give change, and the ID and the expense's place in `history` stay the same.
- If the amount or currency changes without a split option, it's split equally among the people it was split among before, in the same order. That order decides who gets the leftover cents.
- A new currency is converted at its current rate. If only the amount changes, the rate stored with the expense is kept, the same way `add` fixes the rate when an expense is recorded.
- With a split option, `--exact` amounts must add up to the new amount if you change it in the same command.
- If anything is wrong (unknown ID, bad value, missing rate, conflicting split options), nothing is saved.

**`--in CUR`**
- Converts each amount at the current rate and rounds it to the cent, in the same JSON shape as now.
- A currency with no rate is an error, and the base currency gives the usual output.
- For `settle`, the payments are worked out in the base currency first and then each amount is converted, so they're the same payments, just shown in the other currency.

**Choices you may want changed:**
- **Zero shares:** "Same people as before" includes anyone with a 0.00 share. So if an expense was split `--shares A=1,B=0` and you then change the amount, B now pays half. Add a split option to the edit if you don't want that.
- **Converted amounts don't always balance:** because each one is rounded on its own, the converted balances may not add up to exactly zero. Tiny negative amounts show as `0.00` rather than `-0.00`.
- **Edit with no options:** this is an error ("nothing to change") rather than doing nothing silently.

The new logic is mostly `cmd_expense_edit` in `kitty/cli.py`, with small helpers in `kitty/core.py` (`at_rate`, `converter`, `equal_shares`). `settle` now takes an optional currency conversion, and by default its output is unchanged.
